item.title: India remains growth engine; Super El Nino impact yet to materialise: IMF
item.description: The IMF on Thursday said the impact of weather events such as the Super El Nino was yet to materialise for India, which remains the engine of growth for the world economy. The IMF listed lower crop yields, increased food price inflation and its impact on the purchasing power of households in India due to the Super El Nino. "So these are risks that we see that India faces, but right now those risks have not materialised," IMF Communications Director Julie Kozack told a press conference here. She said the IMF will reassess India's growth projections in the January World Economic Outlook update after the risks posed by the weather event materialise. Earlier this month, the IMF raised India's growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7 per cent, from the 6.4 per cent and 6.7 per cent projections respectively made in July. "So, we see it really as a risk going forward, and of course depending on whether that risk materialises, we will reassess our growth projections
item.bs:keywords: El Nino, Indian economy, IMF, inflation, weather events, World Economic Outlook

item.title: Halt in Russian crude imports could raise costs for Indian refiners: Kpler
item.description: A sudden halt to Russian crude imports would pose a supply-chain challenge for Indian refiners, potentially intensifying competition for alternative barrels and putting pressure on freight and procurement costs, while limited scope for further growth in Venezuelan oil output could constrain refiners' ability to exploit cheaper heavy crude, analysts said. Russian crude, which became a significant component of India's oil import basket after the Russia-Ukraine war, has lost some of its earlier pricing appeal as elevated freight costs eroded its advantage on a delivered basis. This has encouraged Indian refiners to look increasingly towards Middle Eastern grades, where shorter shipping routes and competitive delivered economics offer an alternative, according to Sumit Ritolia, senior manager for modelling at commodities intelligence firm Kpler. "Replacing Russian crude at scale is fundamentally a supply-chain challenge rather than simply a question of paying more per barrel," he ...

item.title: US trade deal will protect all sensitive Indian interests: Piyush Goyal
item.description: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday said India's bilateral trade deal with the US would protect all sensitive interests of the country, asserting that people would celebrate the agreement once its details are made public. He said that the opposition parties who are criticising the agreement lack understanding and knowledge about the subject. "The US free trade deal is sometimes sought to be politicised by a few elements... because of lack of understanding and lack of knowledge. Details are not yet fully out...I do not know what they (opposition parties) criticise. "But I have the courage of conviction to announce boldly that the US trade deal, once details are out, the people of India will celebrate that not a single sensitive interest of our commerce or any stakeholder has been compromised. On the contrary, India will stand at a very strong comparative advantage and trade is about comparative advantage," Goyal said here at the ISID-IDRA national conference. In

item.description: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday said Uttar Pradesh is emerging as a major hub for investment, innovation, and industry. He also apprised people of the changes the state has witnessed since 2017 through his social media account on 'X'. Targeting the previous government, Adityanath said, "Before 2017, UP had neither a clear vision nor a concrete action plan to attract global investment. However, the double-engine government changed this situation. "Under the able leadership of PM Narendra Modi, a new work culture for investment and industrial development was developed in the state with the mantra of Reform, Perform and Transform." The Chief Minister said, "With better law and order, transparent policies and an investment-friendly environment, UP is now emerging as a major hub for investment, innovation and industry. "To take this growing global confidence to new heights, today's meeting with the Singapore delegation will discuss new investment opportunities
